intro: Three situations I often deal with for French government ministries and the public sector, presented as I would for a client: the context, my role, what I did and what came out of it. For confidentiality, no client or programme is named and some details have been changed.

etudes.titre: Deciding whether to open a sensitive service
etudes.organisation: Capgemini, for a French government ministry
etudes.contexte: An internal digital service was about to open to new users, some of them outside the ministry's network, with sensitive data at stake. Before deciding, senior management wanted to know the real risks, what it would cost to address them and how that would affect the schedule.
etudes.role: Project manager for the assessment: scoping with the CISO and business teams, running the workshops, summarising for senior management.
enjeux: Speak the language of the business as well as that of security
Get decisions within the project schedule without holding up delivery
Produce a file that can be reused for security accreditation
actions: Business assets, supporting assets and stakeholders mapped with business and operations teams, following the EBIOS Risk Manager method
Strategic and operational scenarios ranked by severity and likelihood
Measures costed in money and time, sorted into three groups: before opening, to schedule, to accept
A short decision note for senior management alongside the full report
resultats: Opening decided in committee, on the basis of identified and explicitly accepted risks
A treatment plan built into the project schedule
A file reused for security accreditation

etudes.titre: Choosing trusted hosting for a sensitive application
etudes.contexte: An existing application had to leave its original hosting. Two paths were open: a SecNumCloud-qualified trusted cloud, or an on-premise deployment at the client's site. The choice would commit the ministry for several years.
etudes.role: Project manager for the architecture study, working with an architect and a security expert.
enjeux: Compare two options on criteria that management can decide on
Meet sovereignty and data protection requirements
Anticipate the full cost: migration, operations, reversibility
Avoid creating a dependency on a supplier that would be hard to undo
actions: Selection criteria and weighting agreed with management before the study
Inventory of the application's data flows, data and dependencies
Two target architectures compared on security, data location, full cost, lead time, operating skills and reversibility
Migration roadmap for the chosen option
resultats: One option chosen and justified before the steering committee
A migration roadmap the teams could work from

etudes.titre: Delivering a business application under security requirements
etudes.organisation: Capgemini, for a French government ministry
etudes.contexte: A business application to build for a ministry's staff, with high security requirements, a tight schedule and a budget of several million euros.
etudes.role: Project manager and project security officer, accountable for the client, the budget, the contract and a multidisciplinary team of five to fifteen people: developers, testers, an architect and a security expert.
enjeux: Hold the schedule and the budget
Build security in from the first iterations
Keep business users at the centre of decisions
actions: Scoping with business teams and splitting the work into deliverable releases
Agile delivery (Scrum) with regular steering meetings with the client
Security requirements tracked in the backlog alongside features, with the accreditation file kept up to date at each release
Dashboard shared with the client: remaining work, budget spent, risks
Financial tracking, contract amendments and risk management
resultats: Releases put into production at a steady pace
A relationship that continued into further phases

annexe.titre: This website, run as a client project
annexe.contexte: A personal website that presents my background to recruiters and partners, with a private area opened by a personal link. I run it to the standards of a client project: milestones, exit criteria and security by design.
annexe.role: Project manager and technical lead: scoping, architecture choices, security requirements, managing development and reviewing every change.
enjeux: Present a background that can be checked, with public source code
Apply to a small project the security standards I advocate on large ones
Keep it simple to host and to develop further
actions: Full scoping before the first line of code: needs, audiences, site structure, architecture and hosting
Four-workstream roadmap, each with a verifiable exit criterion
Monitored delivery pipeline: review of every change, automated tests, code and image scanning, tracked dependencies
Hardened server behind Cloudflare, strict security headers, no third-party trackers
Private area with personal links that expire and can be revoked, tokens stored only as hashes
resultats: Source code and decision history publicly available
Page security and accessibility checked automatically on every change
French and English versions generated from the same data
